boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named campus places for studying, events, arts, recreation, and community participation, documented by Monmouth University and its official athletics program.

cards.title: Rebecca Stafford Student Center
cards.subtitle: Campus gathering, study, and event space
cards.notes: Use the lounges or study areas between commitments, then check the building directory for services, meetings, and scheduled campus programs.
cards.short_summary: A multipurpose campus hub with study areas, student-organization offices, food options, and event spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth identifies the Rebecca Stafford Student Center as a multipurpose gathering facility with lounges/study areas, a computer lab, dining, meeting rooms, and event spaces.
cards.source_title: Rebecca Stafford Student Center | Student Engagement | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: For members of the campus community and their guests; check posted hours and event access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Murry and Leonie Guggenheim Memorial Library
cards.title: Murry and Leonie Guggenheim Memorial Library
cards.subtitle: Library group-study spaces
cards.notes: Bring a partner or project group and use a group study space with a large display monitor; verify the day’s library hours first.
cards.short_summary: The campus library supports group work with accessible study spaces, Wi-Fi, printing, and laptop lending.
cards.evidence_claim: The Monmouth University Library provides group study spaces with large display monitors, Wi-Fi, printing, and laptop lending.
cards.source_title: About | Guggenheim Memorial Library | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: Check the library’s current hours and applicable visitor or room-use policies before arrival.

cards.title: Nagy Common
cards.subtitle: Outdoor patio at the Student Center
cards.notes: Look for campus programming on the patio, or use its seating and firepit area when it is open and not reserved for an event.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor Student Center patio used for programs including performances, s’more nights, sales, and vending events.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth describes Nagy Common as an outdoor patio with seating and a firepit that hosts s’more nights, student performances, poster sales, and vending events.
cards.source_title: Campus Services | Student Handbook | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: Located at the Student Center; use is subject to campus operations and scheduled events.

cards.entity_name: The Great Hall at Shadow Lawn
cards.title: The Great Hall at Shadow Lawn
cards.subtitle: Historic campus landmark and event venue
cards.notes: Pair a look at the landmark’s architecture with a campus event in its auditorium or meeting spaces, where access is available.
cards.short_summary: A National Historic Landmark with classrooms, an auditorium, and spaces used for meetings and events.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth states that the Great Hall has meeting and event spaces on each floor, including a 225-seat auditorium, and was designated a National Historic Landmark in 1985.
cards.source_title: The Historic Great Hall at Shadow Lawn | Conference and Event Services | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: The building contains University offices and reservable spaces; attend according to building and event access rules.

cards.title: Pollak Theatre and Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: Howard Hall performing-arts venue
cards.notes: Check the Center for the Arts calendar for a performance or screening, and allow time to see the gallery outside the auditorium.
cards.short_summary: A 714-seat campus theater with an adjacent gallery, hosting live theater, opera viewings, and other arts programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth says Pollak Theatre hosts live theater performances, MET Opera viewings, and other Center for the Arts programs; Pollak Gallery sits directly outside the auditorium.
cards.source_title: Pollak Theatre | Conference and Event Services | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: Programming, admission, and gallery access vary by event; confirm details with the presenter.

cards.title: OceanFirst Bank Center
cards.subtitle: Campus fitness, recreation, and arena complex
cards.notes: Use the fitness center or indoor track if eligible, or plan around a campus game, ceremony, or other scheduled event in the arena.
cards.short_summary: A campus complex with fitness and leisure spaces, an indoor track, University Store, Hall of Fame, and arena.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth identifies the OceanFirst Bank Center as housing a fitness center, indoor track, University Store, Hall of Fame, meeting/classroom/leisure spaces, and a 4,100-seat arena.
cards.source_title: Campus Services | Student Handbook | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: Fitness and event access can be limited to eligible users or ticket holders; verify current facility rules.

cards.entity_name: Henni Kantor Kessler and John H. Kessler Stadium
cards.title: Kessler Stadium
cards.subtitle: Home venue for Monmouth football and lacrosse
cards.notes: Follow the athletics schedule, bring a valid Monmouth ID if you are a student, and use the designated stadium entrance on game day.
cards.short_summary: The University’s home stadium for football and lacrosse, with student entry managed through Monmouth ID scanning.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth Athletics states that all home lacrosse and football games are played at Kessler Stadium and that students scan a valid student ID for ticketed games.
cards.access_notes: For ticketed events, students must show and scan a valid Monmouth student ID; others may need a ticket.

cards.title: Lois Blonder Sculpture Garden
cards.subtitle: Outdoor art garden beside the 600 Art Building
cards.notes: Take the walking paths slowly and use the sculptures, pond, and plantings as prompts for a short outdoor art or photography break.
cards.short_summary: A campus art garden with walking paths, a koi pond, plants, and sculptures from Lois Blonder’s collection.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth reports that the Lois Blonder Sculpture Garden beside the 600 Art Building includes a koi pond, walking paths, plants, and an array of sculptures.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and any temporary campus restrictions may affect access.

cards.title: Erlanger Gardens
cards.subtitle: Garden grounds at the Great Hall
cards.notes: Walk the fountains and portico beside the Great Hall, then use the garden for a quiet study or relaxation pause when no event is using it.
cards.short_summary: A landscaped Great Hall garden with fountains and a portico, described by the University as a place for events, studying, and relaxation.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth’s campus map describes Erlanger Gardens as a flower-and-shrub garden with fountains and a portico that serves campus events, studying, and relaxation.
cards.source_title: Garden Archives | Campus Map | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: The garden can be incorporated into Great Hall events; yield to scheduled use and observe posted campus guidance.

cards.title: Virginia A. Cory Community Garden
cards.subtitle: 19 Beechwood Avenue community volunteer garden
cards.notes: Join an organized volunteer activity to plant, maintain, harvest, or support donations; review the garden’s current participation information before going.
cards.short_summary: A School of Social Work-supported garden where University and community participants grow produce and support local donations.
cards.evidence_claim: Monmouth describes the Virginia A. Cory Community Garden as a cooperative volunteer effort involving students, faculty, and community members that offers gardening and donation work.
cards.source_title: Virginia A. Cory Community Garden | Monmouth University
cards.access_notes: Volunteer participation is welcomed, while garden plots have application and annual-fee requirements; consult current garden guidance.
